name: Squat
pattern: Knee-dominant squat: hips, knees and ankles bend together on two feet, then drive up to standing.
setup: Feet about shoulder width, toes turned out a little (about 15-30°).
Bar on your upper back (or weight held at your chest), elbows under it.
Big breath into your belly and brace before each rep.

steps.text: Stand tall, weight over the middle of your feet.
Bend hips and knees together, knees moving out over your toes.
Sit down until your hip crease is level with or just below your knees, back still flat.
Push the floor away with your whole foot; hips and chest rise at the same rate.

cues.cue: Knees track over your toes, not inward.
cues.why: Knees caving in is the most common fault and puts sideways stress on the knee.

cues.cue: Whole foot down: heel, big toe, little toe.
cues.why: Stiff ankles make the heels rise and the knees cave; raise your heels on plates if needed.

cues.cue: Brace and keep your back flat to the bottom.
cues.why: A braced, neutral spine handles the load; rounding at the bottom raises stress on the lower back.

cues.cue: Thighs to parallel or below, if your back stays flat.
cues.why: Full squats grew the glutes and adductors more than half squats, and do not raise knee risk with good form.

cues.cue: Let your knees pass your toes if your heels stay down.
cues.why: Holding the knees back cut knee load a little but raised hip load and forward lean a lot.

cues.cue: Pick the width and toe-out that lets you sit deep.
cues.why: Wider stances and more toe-out shift load toward the hips; both are fine choices.

breathing: Breathe in and brace at the top, hold it on the way down, breathe out past the hardest part on the way up.

tempo.note: Lower under control in about 2 seconds, stand up in 1.

mistakes.name: Knees cave in
mistakes.looks: The knees move inside the line of the feet, often on the way up.
mistakes.fix: Push your knees out over your little toes; lighten the load.
mistakes.why: Weak or late hip abductors let the thigh roll in, which stresses the knee.

mistakes.name: Heels lift
mistakes.looks: The heels come off the floor and weight shifts to the toes.
mistakes.fix: Sit back a little more, or squat with your heels on small plates.
mistakes.why: Limited ankle bend; it pushes the bar forward and the knees inward.

mistakes.name: Lower back rounds at the bottom
mistakes.looks: The pelvis tucks under and the lower back curls at the deepest point.
mistakes.fix: Stop just above the depth where your back starts to round, and brace harder.
mistakes.why: Rounding under load moves stress from the muscles to the discs and ligaments.

mistakes.name: Hips shoot up first
mistakes.looks: On the way up the hips rise but the chest stays down, turning the squat into a bend-over.
mistakes.fix: Lead with your chest; hips and shoulders rise together.
mistakes.why: It moves the work off the quads onto the lower back.

safety: Use safety pins or spotter arms set just below your bottom position with a barbell.
Knee pain: shorten the depth to a box and keep the shins more upright.
Back pain: try a goblet or front squat, which keep the trunk more upright.
High blood pressure: avoid long breath holds; breathe out on each rep.

variants.change: Weight in front: trunk more upright (about 20-30° at the bottom), similar muscle work, less compressive load on the knee.
Bar lower on the back: more trunk lean and more hip load.
Bar high on the traps: trunk more upright, deeper knees.
Sit to a box or pins: shins more vertical, depth set by the box.
Wide stance, toes out 30-45°: more hip and adductor load, trunk more upright.
Feet hip width or closer: more knee bend, harder on ankle mobility.
Partial range: knees bent only about 45-90°.
Heels on a wedge: knees travel further forward, more quads, easier for stiff ankles.
Pause 2 seconds at the bottom, staying braced.
Bar on a fixed path: feet can go a little in front; balance is not trained.
Bands or chains make the top harder; same keyframes.
Stand on plates for extra depth.
Squat then press the weight overhead as you stand (thruster).

subtypes.name: Wall sit
subtypes.match: sit \(wall\)|wall sit|wall squat|wall slide|ball wall|on the wall|stability ball wall
subtypes.change: Back flat on the wall, feet forward, thighs level, held still. Tracking: hold. Repeated wall-sit holds of about 2 minutes lowered resting blood pressure in a home training study.

subtypes.name: Front or goblet squat
subtypes.change: Weight held at the chest or front of the shoulders; trunk stays more upright. A front squat is more upright than a back squat with similar muscle work and less knee compression; a low-bar back squat leans the most.

subtypes.name: Sumo squat
subtypes.change: Feet wide, toes out, weight hangs between the legs; knees push out hard.

subtypes.name: Overhead squat
subtypes.change: Arms locked overhead, wide grip if using a bar; needs an upright trunk and mobile shoulders.

subtypes.name: Box squat
subtypes.change: Sit back to a box at about knee height, touch without relaxing, stand up; shins stay near vertical.

metrics.label: Knee inside the foot line (front view)
Trunk lean
metrics.good: 20-30 front squat, 35-50 back squat at the bottom

motion.basis: Depth ranges from schoenfeld2010, hartmann2013 and kubo2019; trunk lean by bar position from glassbrook2017 and gullett2009; stance and toe-out from lorenzetti2018. Exact keyframe angles are estimates for an average adult high-bar squat to just below parallel. Arm angles estimated for a back-squat grip.
